title: The Requisition
description: Brasston's curator keeps the column. It never forbids anything — it simply declines to fund it, which in this district is the same thing arriving by a politer road.

steps.text: The top street was stacked to the shopfronts with crates, and every crate was stencilled APPROVED on one side and HELD on the other, so that whether a thing was coming or going depended entirely on which way round somebody had set it down. Between two of the stacks a ledger stood open on a frame at reading height, and the figures in it were being added to while the party watched.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: ENTRY NOTED. Against which line is this to be charged?

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: Passage is a line. Everything is a line. A thing with no line does not move.

lines.speaker: Rogue
lines.text: Half this street is crates nobody ever came back for.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: Held, not refused. Nothing here was ever refused. There is no stamp for refused.

lines.speaker: Mage
lines.text: Then say yes. If you can't say no, say yes.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: Approval is not withheld. Approval is UNFUNDED. The column does not balance for this.

lines.speaker: Bard
lines.text: You've built a wall out of arithmetic so nobody can be blamed for it.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: Blame is also a line. It has never been funded either.

lines.speaker: Fighter
lines.text: Then we'll take it out of your column ourselves.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: An unauthorised draw. Those are also recorded. PROCEED, AND IT WILL BE RECORDED.
